source.title: Transformer protein language models are unsupervised structure learners
source.authors: Roshan Rao; Joshua Meier; Tom Sercu; S. Ovchinnikov; Alexander Rives

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether downstream contact-prediction performance in protein language models relates to pretraining perplexity, extending the question to protein models and a protein-structure task.
record.gate_note: The study reports contact-precision results and a validation-perplexity/contact-precision relationship. It does not fit or test power laws for language-model loss, make small-run loss predictions, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its mention of scaling laws in the discussion is not itself a result on those claims.
record.test_reason: Protein masked language models. The study reports long-range contact precision (a downstream task) against held-out validation perplexity over pretraining, and across ESM-1 sizes of 43M, 85M and 670M parameters trained on the same data. This bears on V6 in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. The authors find a linear link between validation perplexity and contact precision, with ESM-1 12- and 34-layer models matching at equal perplexity. They conclude both scale and hyperparameters matter, and that scaling-law evidence supports growing protein LMs. Their scaling-law language in the discussion is an analogy to Kaplan et al., not a power-law fit.
record.recipe_differences: Protein masked-language-model pretraining and contact prediction; measures a downstream protein-structure task and perplexity/contact-precision association, not text-model held-out loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The ESM-1 and ESM-1b masking patterns differ, making their perplexities incomparable; the authors also note architecture and hyperparameters affect contact learning.
record.problems: The perplexity/contact-precision relationship is shown in a figure without tabulated values. The paper cautions that ESM-1 and ESM-1b perplexities are not directly comparable because their masking patterns differ. Models also differ in dataset, architecture, and other hyperparameters, complicating cross-model scale comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contact-precision values are included. Other contact-prediction ablations and CASP13 results are not extracted because they do not report the perplexity-versus-downstream-performance relationship or a scale comparison used for V6.

untested.parts: No fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fixed-size shape sweep measuring loss.
No power-law fit of protein LM loss.
Only one downstream task family (contacts) and three same-data sizes. No functional fit or extrapolation of downstream performance to larger models.

missing.what: Contact-probability calibration improves with scale: MSE 0.074, 0.028, 0.020 for ESM-1 6/12/34 layers, and 0.014 for ESM-1b.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Table 1 rows within the ESM-1 family form a clean same-data size series. TAPE and ProtBERT rows are confounded by dataset and architecture. The reader's limits_scope label on masking incomparability was replaced by one based on the ESM-1b vs ESM-1 34-layer gap at similar size.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or test of held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
No prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or parameter/token growth exponents.
No controlled comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count measuring loss.
Protein models and fine-tuning are studied, but no test of the same power-law form across modalities or training regimes.

Tests contact-prediction performance against validation perplexity and across several pretrained model sizes; it does not test predictability across other downstream tasks or language-model families generally.
No analysis of fitted scaling exponents, compute-optimal allocation fits, or departures from a single loss power law.

relationships.condition: Within each ESM model's pretraining trajectory, and across ESM-1 sizes on the same data
relationships.reason: The authors report a linear perplexity–long-range P@L relationship for each model, and 12- and 34-layer models match at equal perplexity (t55–t58). Long-range P@L rises 13.2→23.7→34.7 with size (t25, t34, t43).
relationships.display_finding: Long-range P@L varied linearly with perplexity within each model, matched between 12- and 34-layer models at equal perplexity, and increased 13.2→23.7→34.7 with size.

relationships.condition: Across model families or hyperparameter settings at similar parameter count
relationships.reason: ESM-1b at 650M reaches 41.1 long-range P@L versus 34.7 for ESM-1 at 670M. Downstream performance depends on hyperparameters, not parameter count alone (t43, t52).
relationships.display_finding: ESM-1b at 650M achieves long-range P@L of 41.1 versus 34.7 for ESM-1 at 670M, showing that hyperparameters affect performance beyond parameter count.
